units.translation: 1 Basil, Serm. de leg. libr. gent. 3; Mant. prov. III 15
1 τάν in PH : τὴν in L : τόν in V; σπάρτον in L : -αν in P : -ην in V
327. νηὸς ἑῆς προτέρῳ: incorrectly uses ἑῆς for a plural; for it is singular. He should have said σφετέρης.
331. 〈μετά:〉 instead of εἰς. Lg
335. σφωιτέρῃ: incorrectly used σφωιτέρῃ for a singular; for it is dual. Jason traces his lineage from Aeolus, as Hellanicus (4 fg 128 J.) says.

336-39a. στεῦται ἀμειλίκτοιο: the sense: he declares that the descendants of Aeolus will not escape the implacable wrath of Zeus nor the pollution and the penalty for Phrixus, until the fleece is brought to Greece. The order: στεῦται δ’ Αἰολιδῶν γενεὴν οὐχ ὑπαλύξειν ἀμειλίκτοιο Διὸς μῆνιν καὶ χόλον, πρὶν ἐς Ἑλλάδα 〈κῶας〉 ἱκέσθαι.
14 added by K
b. ποινάς: punishments. Lg (P)
342a. We got the worst of the Colchian ships. Lm (P)
b. ἤλιθα: in abundance. LgP
349. 〈εἴ:〉 in order that. Sm
350. 〈αὐτῷ:〉 instead of σοί. Lg
354-55. δῆθεν is redundant. But if you wish, he says, to know the lineage and name of each, I would recount them all. L
20 παρέλκεται τὸ δῆθεν in Lm
21 supplied by K
356. 〈οἷό περ:〉 for whose sake. Lg

359. 〈γνωτός:〉 instead of kinsman or cousin, first cousin. Cretheus and Athamas are brothers, sons of Aeolus; Aeson is son of Cretheus, Jason son of Aeson, Phrixus son of Athamas, and Argus his son. Lm
23 ἤγουν instead of ἢ in A
368a. ἠερέθοντο: they were raised up in their angry mind, instead of they were swelling. Lm (P)
27 οἰδαίνοντο in P : -ετο in L
b. 〈ὑψοῦ δὲ χόλῳ φρένες ἠερέθοντο:〉 he was gnashing, he was puffing up. Lm
28 sch. b separated from a by W
29 ἐφυσιοῦτο in A : -σκοῦτο in L : -σσοῦτο in F
375-76a. 〈αὐτίκα:〉 instead of now. Lg
b. νέεσθαι: ἔολπα is to be understood from the common construction. Lg (P)
2 at νέεσθαι the scholiast wants ἔολπα to be supplied from ἐώλπει in line 370
3 lemma in P : omitted in L
386. σχέο μοι: O Aeetes, restrain or endure me concerning this expedition.
388. τὸ δὲ οὐδὲ μὲν ἱέμενοι instead of not even desiring your kingdom. P
395-96. Incorrectly used σφωιτέροισιν for a singular; for he should have said τεοῖσιν. And ἴσκεν is used in Homeric fashion.
7 τῷ in Steph.
399. τὸ δὲ πειρήσαιτο βίην instead of he might make trial of the strength of the heroes. P
400-01. Incorrectly uses ὑποβλήδην; for it is used before the other has finished speaking. And διηνεκέως ἀγορεύεις instead of you speak at length.
404-06a. 〈δώσω:〉 having made trial of your courage I will give the fleece; for it is not my way to begrudge. L
14 sch. a, which adheres to sch. b, separated by W
b. 〈οὔτι μεγαίρω:〉 instead of I do not begrudge you, like Pelias.
408a. 〈τόν:〉 the contest. Lg
18 τὸν μέγαν in W : τὸ μέγα
409-10. δοιώ μοι πεδίον τὸ Ἀρή〈ιον: ...〉 and Antimachus in his Lyde (fg 9 B. II 290) represented the bulls as made by Hephaestus.
19 sch. Pind. Pyth. IV 398 c
